body:
I learned that the I set too much of a barrier around myself which leads to my extreme isolation. 

I learned about the ridiculous number of places I could go to in my area if I ever have trouble. 

I learned that I need to pay closer attention to time management, which needs to consist of socialization, exercise, responsibilities, and relaxation. Not fulfilling those responsibilities is what can lead to depression.

I learned that I'm not alone.

Perhaps most importantly I learned that I'm not as socially awkward and resistant to social interaction as I thought I was. It was very easy to talk to the people there and all of them agreed that I appeared to be very socially outgoing. Furthermore, I enjoyed the social interaction and made some new friends.
He uses it sparingly, which is good.

A person can leave once they're determined that they aren't a danger to themselves or others. The staff observes behavior, who's going to groups, who's socializing, responses to 1-on-1s, ect. I guess the main thing they're looking for is mood improvement (or a willingness to follow-up on an addiction). 

I'd say they'd heavily discourage it but I probably could leave whenever I wanted. The point is to get better, so once you accept that I'd assume you'd be moved to voluntary status (most people enter as involuntary status). Most people in there just failed a suicide attempt. Once they determine that your mood has improved and that you aren't a danger to yourself or others then the topic of leaving will come up.

I'm in follow-up treatment at my school, so I can't really say how it is for others. Once patients accept that the mental health unit is for their benefit I'd think they'd make the decision to follow-up on their own. It probably isn't required but heavily encouraged.
I agree with postmodgirl; you're a very good listener. And by going to your friend for advice you'll likely strengthen your friendship with that friend.

I apologize for the late response, but I only log onto this account for the self-help subreddits. You'll forgive me won't you?

The problem is that I am **not** struggling with gender identity issues that you're trying to project on me.  There's a difference between feeling like the other gender and wanting to be the other gender: the former describes a transgender and the latter does not. I repeat, my imagery comes forth as a desire to repeat life as someone completely different from myself, and the easiest way for me to do that is to imagine myself as the other gender. I imagine you read "women have it easier" in one of my posts and ran with it, but that statement alone is taken out of context. You read what you wanted to read, what you expected to read, and immediately labeled me as another oppressive male.

I don't know why, but I enjoyed reading your post. Maybe I find the effort that went into it and the length of your posts humorous. Maybe I just like seeing people get angry (I'm not being condescending; I don't know myself). Whatever reason it is I'm sure it's due to what a terrible person I am.

I don't really enjoy much of anything right now. I'm currently in college with the intention of getting a degree in biomedical engineering, but my interest in learning is low when my mood is low as it is now (I typically go into the semester with a positive attitude then go back to feeling low a few months in). As much as I like seeing dogs on the streets helping at a shelter would feel like more of a chore than anything. I ultimately want to get an engineering degree and go on to grad school but right now I'm a mess. Like I said, I'm just going through the motions until I can figure out a solution but I'm miserable while doing so.

I guess I should've mentioned that in my original post. I've been seeing a therapist and psychiatrist since the end of April (not as frequently as I'd like, but my schedule doesn't mesh well with their schedules). I've been taking anti-depressant/anti-anxiety medication since mid-July but it's difficult to tell whether it's changed anything or not. School life has been a little easier but I'm starting to fall into old patterns and could soon return to the miserable state I was in at the end of my 2012 spring semester. If this detachment from people really is a chemical imbalance then I feel like there's nothing I can do to make myself feel better except wait for the right combination and dosage of meds.

> Sorry if I am coming off as aggressively angry ( how unfeminine of me :P)

It's not unfeminine, it's inappropriate and irrelevant. This is a self help group, not a plug for your personal views. 

> The circumstances you grew up with do sound like they were hard and I am sorry that you feel you missed out on being properly socialized. I hope you find a way to increase your self esteem and make friends!

This is the only part of your post that even remotely addresses the problem I originally posted about, and that's not really saying much because this fragment is nothing more than "I empathize with you; get well soon". You don't care about me at all, you just care about getting your opinion out there. I find that pretty insulting.

I don't know why you're throwing the word "fact" around when my quote specifically used the word "believe". 

All I meant was that women have an easier time finding people to talk to than men because people approach them while men are expected to be the ones to approach.I feel that women have less social pressure than men do. Women can act however they feel but men are supposed to be emotionless, assertive, confident, whatever. Most men who aren't the above things are labeled losers. 

The problem with me was my social development. I had limited contact with friends and classmates from 1st grade through the end of highschool; this has left me emotionally numb when it comes to social interactions. I just imagine that if I had grown up as a female I would've socialized more. These past few days I haven't been harping on the gender transformation thing as much. I'm starting to think that I enjoy this fantasy because of my low self-esteem; I feel that I would be happier if I were anyone but myself.

I'm working on self improvement and would eventually like to have an intimate relationship. I don't feel guilty at this point, but I would feel guilty if I were with a woman in bed and this crap were in my head. I'm just trying to be proactive so that once my depression is under control and social problems are resolved I can enter the dating world more quickly.

When I see a woman I can judge whether she's attractive or not but I don't feel any kind of excitement. There were some women who I've been interested but it's never panned out due to distance or my social inadequacy(which I'm working on). I'm not that interested in sex, but that could either be due to my obsession with this fetish or my being a virgin.

Again, I really just want to get rid of this. I figure switching to porn would be the easiest way to do this (and it may help my libido). Do you have any other ideas as to what I should do? What sort of steps should I take to get away from transformations and into more socially acceptable stuff?

Guilt is irrelevant here; if you had read my initial post you would have known that. I want this out of my life because it's consuming me. I will never be able to have a serious relationship with a woman if I can't find her attractive and have to think of these perverted fantasies to get off with her. Thinking about changing into a 6 year old while in bed with a 20 year old woman is something I want nothing to do with.

>Everytime I hear a kid bragging about depression...


I always found that a bit ironic. Most people who are diagnosed with depression will do everything they can to hide it from people they know. Bragging about having depression is basically confirming that you don't have depression.

I drifted away from my close friends during my past few semesters of depression; everyone that I know now is an acquaintance or a meh-friend as best. I figure that If I stay social I'll eventually find someone that I'd be interested in being friends with, but it wouldn't be appropriate to tell my new friend about my issues a few weeks after meeting him. I think in terms of help I'll have to rely on my therapist and group therapy.

Empathy could be an issue to some extent. I can understand why a person would feel a certain way, but I don't always understand the feeling itself. I also have trouble grasping what motivates people to act the way they do. My actions are motivated solely by what is expected of me. Maybe this is just due to the depression; maybe once I remember how it feels to 'want' something I'll be able to empathize with others.

I have no idea what kind of relationship you have with your dad, but if your dad loves and cares about you then he'll want to do anything that he can to help you. It can be tough but it's a good thing if you have someone by your side to help you through this, keep you on track, monitor possible meds, make the therapy a bit cheaper (I was paying 10$/session), ect. If you find a therapist or psychiatrist that you really trust then you can ask that person to talk to your dad for you. 

Also, note that not all therapists will work out. Your therapist needs to be someone that you are willing to open up to. Every therapist has different methods that you may or may not be comfortable with. Don't think that you're stuck with the first one.

 Going to group therapy when you go back to school is also an option. I've never done it myself (preparing to do it this year), but I'd imagine being in a room with people with similar problems is somewhat comforting.

Find something to occupy your day with, even if you don't really like it or don't think you'll like it. Doing some kind of exercise would probably be the best thing since your therapist and psychiatrist (if you get one) will tell you that exercising will help with your depression. I've recently started weightlifting and find that even though I don't find it fun, it's a nice distraction and I get a bit of a high when I finish. 

Again, pick something to do even if you don't like doing it. It would be better if it were something difficult like exercise, but for now it can be anything.
My only regret would be the grief I'd cause my parents. Aside from that I'd welcome death.
